title: Inverse image on bounded below derived categories
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and let $u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\to\Ab(U_{\Et})$ be the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], an exact functor [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]. The *inverse image on the bounded below derived categories*

$$
 u^{-1}:\Dplus(V_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Dplus(U_{\Et})
$$

[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] is the restriction to $\Dplus(V_{\Et})$ of the triangulated functor $D(V_{\Et})\to D(U_{\Et})$ induced by applying $u^{-1}$ termwise to cochain complexes [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; it takes values in $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Thus no resolution is used: if a bounded below complex $K^\bullet$ represents $K$, then the complex $u^{-1}K^\bullet=(u^{-1}K^r)_r$ represents $u^{-1}K$, through the natural isomorphism $u^{-1}(Q K^\bullet)\cong Q(u^{-1}K^\bullet)$ of the induced functor, $Q$ denoting the localization functors to the derived categories. As $u^{-1}$ is exact, this functor is also its right and left derived functor, and is written $u^{-1}$ rather than $Lu^{-1}$. With a fixed coefficient ring whose pullback is identified with itself, the same construction applies to module sheaves.

source.place: Section 0735 (section-base-change-map), paragraph before Lemma 0736: an exact pullback g^* has a derived functor on D computed by pulling back any representative (Derived Categories, Lemma 015F) and preserves the bounded (above, below) subcategories; it is written g^* rather than Lg^*
